key_insight: Backward quadrature learning (BQL) learns quadrature for Brownian increments within BSDE backward recursion to solve high-dimensional parametric semilinear parabolic PDEs.
engineering_relevance: BQL can reduce amortized computational cost when PDE solutions are needed across multiple parameter queries.
method: Learn Brownian-increment quadrature at each time level to approximate local conditional expectations.
Transfer value-function information backward using a continuation surrogate, avoiding nested quadrature.
Derive a global error decomposition and prove first-order mean-square convergence under suitable assumptions.
evidence_signal: On the HJB benchmark across tested dimensions, the abstract reports competitive accuracy and approximately 40× and 4× computational cost reductions versus P²INN and FBSNN, respectively, for seven parameter queries.
watch_item: Convergence depends on approximation and integrability assumptions, and the reported cost advantages should not be assumed to generalize beyond the tested benchmarks and query counts.
paper_title: Learning the Brownian Motion in Machine Learning for Parametric Parabolic PDEs: A Backward Quadrature Approach
